output_json.patch_notes: In ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(String), changed `path = UriPath.canonical(path)` to `path = UriPath.canonical(path.replace('\\', '/'))` and added a `if (path == null) return null;` guard. Normalizing backslashes to forward slashes before canonicalization ensures backslash traversal segments ('..\\') are seen and collapsed/rejected by canonical(), which returns null when the path escapes above root. Added regression test testGetResource_whenPathUsesBackslashTraversal_thenReturnNull asserting getResource("/..\\secret.txt") returns null. Verified: POV now exits 1 ("traversal blocked"); existing ExternalResourceHandlerTest (7) and UriPathTest (5) all pass.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only affects request paths containing backslashes or that resolve above the base root — both of which are invalid for legitimate URL-based static file serving. Forward-slash paths are unaffected (path.replace is a no-op for them), and legitimate '.'/'..' handling within the base is unchanged since canonical() already handled it. No API, dependency, or behavioral changes for valid requests. Note: sibling handlers (e.g. ClassPathResourceHandler) were not modified as they were out of scope for this alert; if they share the same UriPath usage they may warrant a similar review.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in ExternalResourceHandler.getResource(). Backslash-based traversal paths (e.g. "/..\secret.txt") bypassed the only defense — UriPath.canonical() — which treats only '/' as a separator, and were later collapsed by StringUtils.cleanPath() (which converts '\'→'/' and resolves '..'), escaping the served base directory. The fix normalizes backslashes to forward slashes before canonicalization and rejects paths that canonicalize above root (canonical() returns null), so the handler now returns null instead of serving an out-of-base file.
